c.tagline: Tropical gateway to the Great Barrier Reef and the Daintree rainforest.

taxi.fareNote: Cairns Taxis is the main operator; fares are metered with higher night and airport rates, and rideshare is widely available and often cheaper.

emergency.note: 000 is the primary emergency number for police, fire and ambulance; 112 also works from any mobile and 106 is the text-based line for the deaf or speech-impaired.

avoid.reason: The Esplanade nightclub strip sees alcohol-fuelled trouble late at night; also heed stinger and crocodile signage rather than crime worries.

hood_desc: The compact waterfront heart around the Esplanade, the saltwater swimming Lagoon, the Reef Fleet Terminal and the Night Markets; best for first-timers who want reef tours, dining and nightlife on the doorstep.
An inner residential suburb just north of the centre near the hospital and Aeroglen, with quieter streets, motels and easy airport access; good value within a short walk or bus of the Esplanade.
A leafy foothill suburb around the Cairns Botanic Gardens and the Whitfield rainforest walks, with a small strip of cafes; suits travelers wanting green calm over the tourist strip.
A relaxed Northern Beaches village about 15 km north with a palm-lined swimming beach, esplanade cafes and holiday apartments; a laid-back base away from the city.
The most upscale of the Northern Beaches, a resort village about 25 km north with a paperbark-lined esplanade, boutique resorts and spa retreats; suits couples wanting a polished beach stay.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink in Cairns.

transit.pay: Pay the cash fare to the driver or tap on with a go card (the Queensland TransLink smartcard); Cairns sits in TransLink's regional network and a single adult fare is a few dollars by zone. There is no train, tram or ferry city transit.
transit.hours: Sunbus routes run roughly 6am to around 11pm on core lines (routes 110/111 link the city, the airport turn-off and the Northern Beaches), with limited late-night and Sunday service; taxis and rideshare cover the rest.
transit.note: Cairns has no rail, tram or ferry public transport — Sunbus is the sole network, radiating from the City Place interchange along the Esplanade and up to the Northern Beaches, so many visitors rely on tours, rideshare or a rental car.

landmarks: Cairns Esplanade Lagoon
A free saltwater swimming lagoon fringed by palm trees and boardwalks along the waterfront, perfect for sunset photos.
Great Barrier Reef
The world's largest coral reef system, accessible from Cairns and offering unparalleled snorkelling, diving, and aerial photography.
Skyrail Rainforest Cableway
A breathtaking gondola ride soaring above ancient Daintree rainforest canopy between Cairns and Kuranda.
Kuranda Scenic Railway
A historic heritage train winding through rainforest, gorges, and waterfalls on its way to the mountain village of Kuranda.
Cairns Botanic Gardens
A tropical botanical garden showcasing lush rainforest boardwalks, lily ponds, and exotic flora unique to the wet tropics.
Cape Tribulation
Where the Daintree Rainforest meets the Great Barrier Reef, offering dramatic beaches framed by dense jungle.
Palm Cove Beach
An idyllic palm-lined beach village north of Cairns, famous for its calm waters and giant paperbark trees.
Cairns Aquarium
A modern aquarium showcasing the extraordinary marine life of the Great Barrier Reef and tropical rainforest ecosystems.
Trinity Beach
A relaxed, scenic northern beach suburb with a long sandy shoreline and views toward forested headlands.
Cairns Marina and Waterfront
The bustling gateway to reef and rainforest tours, lined with yachts, restaurants, and sweeping views of the coastal mountains.

train.note: There are no international trains in Australia, and Cairns is the northern terminus of the Queensland coastal line. The Spirit of Queensland links Cairns with Townsville, Rockhampton and Brisbane five times a week, taking about 25 hours for the full run - it leaves Cairns on Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Sunday mornings and offers reclining seats or lie-flat RailBeds. Cairns station sits inside the Cairns Central shopping centre, an easy walk from the Esplanade. Two tourist lines also start here: the Kuranda Scenic Railway up the Barron Gorge (daily, about 1 hr 45 min each way) and the Savannahlander railmotor out to Forsayth on Wednesdays, which does not operate between December and March.

bus.note: No international coaches serve Australia. Greyhound Australia (https://www.greyhound.com.au/) is the main long-distance operator, running south along the Bruce Highway to Townsville (about 6 hours), Airlie Beach, Rockhampton and Brisbane (around 29 hours), and inland to Charters Towers and Mount Isa. Coaches pick up near Cairns Central station and the Reef Fleet Terminal end of the city; book online, as backpacker corridor services fill quickly in the dry season. Trans North Bus runs the regional services up onto the Atherton Tablelands and north to Cooktown.

ferry.note: Cairns has no international or long-distance passenger ferries; the Reef Fleet Terminal on the Marlin Marina is a five-minute walk from the city centre and handles island and Great Barrier Reef boats. Fitzroy Island is about 45 minutes away with several return sailings a day, and Green Island is roughly 45-50 minutes. Sailings are weather-dependent and are occasionally cancelled in the November-April wet and cyclone season. Sea Swift's ships to the Torres Strait from Cairns are freight vessels and should not be relied on for passenger travel.
